name: Local Legal-Market Signal Scanner

parameters.content:
## Local Legal-Market Signal Scanner

### Internal Protomated tool — Authority pillar, powers BD and pipeline

Demand signals for a practice area are public but never collected -- a new business license, a building permit, an entity filing can all mean a new prospect. This watches a configurable public open-data feed (business filings, permits, licenses) and tags each new record against the practice areas it might create demand for, so BD conversations start from an actual signal instead of a cold list.

### How it works

1. Runs daily. Queries a configured public open-data API (built against the common Socrata SODA API pattern used by most city/county/state open-data portals) for records filed since the last run.
2. Normalizes each record's fields using a firm-configured field-name map, since every open-data dataset names its columns differently.
3. Dedupes against signals already seen (no database -- workflow static data, same pattern used throughout this catalog).
4. Tags each new signal against a configurable practice-area keyword map -- a signal can suggest demand for more than one practice area, or none, in which case it's dropped.
5. Logs matched signals and emails a digest to the BD reviewer.
6. Separately, a weekly rollup reports signal volume and top signal types by practice area over the trailing week.

**This monitors and tags public information only -- it is never a legal or business assessment of any specific entity, and it never contacts anyone on the firm's behalf.** It surfaces a public record and a keyword match, nothing more (ABA Op. 512 doesn't directly apply since this isn't law-firm-facing, but the same discipline is kept).

### Before you start: there's no single canonical API for this

Business filing and permit data is scattered across thousands of separate city/county/state open-data portals with no unified national API. This template is built against the Socrata SODA API pattern (used by NYC Open Data, Chicago Data Portal, Austin Open Data, and hundreds of others) since it's the most common standard -- but you need to find and configure a real dataset URL and its actual field names for your target market. If your target jurisdiction doesn't publish on a Socrata portal, this template's HTTP call will need adjusting to that portal's own API shape.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Find a real Socrata-based open-data dataset for business filings/permits/licenses in your target market.
- [ ] Create a Google Sheet with a 'Signal Log' tab -- see the deploy guide for exact columns.
- [ ] Configure Google Sheets OAuth2 and SMTP credentials.
- [ ] Set the required n8n Variables: SIGNAL_DATA_API_URL, SIGNAL_DATE_FIELD, SIGNAL_ID_FIELD, SIGNAL_TYPE_FIELD, SIGNAL_NAME_FIELD, SIGNAL_KEYWORDS_BY_PRACTICE_AREA, BD_REVIEWER_EMAIL, FIRM_FROM_EMAIL, SIGNAL_LOG_SHEET_ID.
- [ ] Optionally tune SIGNAL_LOOKBACK_DAYS, SIGNAL_ADDRESS_FIELD, SIGNAL_LINK_FIELD, SIGNAL_DATA_APP_TOKEN.
- [ ] Activate the workflow.

### Customization

The SIGNAL_*_FIELD variables and SIGNAL_KEYWORDS_BY_PRACTICE_AREA are the entire data-mapping and tagging surface -- edit those n8n Variables, not the code, when you point this at a new dataset.

## Query, normalize, and dedupe

Pulls recent records from a configured open-data API, normalizes the dataset-specific field names, and drops anything already seen on a prior run.

## Tag, log, and draft the daily signal digest

Tags each new signal against a configurable practice-area keyword map, logs matches, and emails a digest -- always sends something, even a 'nothing new' notice.

## Weekly signal volume rollup — a second, independent branch

Aggregates the trailing week's logged signals into a practice-area mix and top signal types, so BD can see patterns beyond one signal at a time.

nodes.name: If Data Source Configured
nodes.notes: Checked here, while there's still guaranteed exactly one item from the trigger -- an unconfigured SIGNAL_DATA_API_URL routes to a setup-needed notice instead of the run silently dying at zero items.

nodes.name: Build Signal Query URL
nodes.notes: SIGNAL_LOOKBACK_DAYS controls the query window -- defaults to 1 (yesterday's filings), since this runs daily.

nodes.name: Fetch New Signal Records
nodes.notes: Most Socrata portals work without an App Token for light traffic, but a daily scheduled poll should use one to avoid throttling -- get a free one from the specific portal's developer settings and set SIGNAL_DATA_APP_TOKEN.

nodes.name: Normalize Signal Records
nodes.notes: SIGNAL_ID_FIELD / SIGNAL_TYPE_FIELD / SIGNAL_NAME_FIELD / SIGNAL_ADDRESS_FIELD / SIGNAL_LINK_FIELD are your dataset's actual column names -- check the portal's API docs (usually an 'API' or 'export' tab on the dataset page) and set these to match.

nodes.name: Dedupe Against Previously Seen Signals
nodes.notes: Uses n8n's workflow static data, not an external database, to remember which signal IDs have already been logged -- consistent with this catalog's established dedupe pattern.

nodes.name: Tag Signals By Practice Area
nodes.notes: SIGNAL_KEYWORDS_BY_PRACTICE_AREA controls which signals are worth surfacing -- a signal matching nothing configured is dropped rather than logged.

nodes.name: Log New Signals For Tracking
nodes.notes: One row per matched signal. Column headers must match exactly.

nodes.name: Draft Signal Digest
nodes.notes: Groups matched signals by practice area -- the same signal can appear under multiple areas if it matched keywords in more than one.

parameters.jsCode: return [{ json: { signal_count: 0, area_count: 0, digest_content: '(no data source configured yet -- set SIGNAL_DATA_API_URL in n8n Variables)', signals_by_area: [] } }];

nodes.name: Draft Setup-Needed Notice
nodes.notes: Fires only when SIGNAL_DATA_API_URL is empty -- keeps the digest email showing up on schedule even before a real data source is configured.

nodes.name: Build Signal Digest Email
nodes.notes: Falls back the recipient to FIRM_FROM_EMAIL if BD_REVIEWER_EMAIL isn't set.

nodes.name: Send Signal Digest Email
nodes.notes: Internal Protomated/BD notification, not a client communication — no compliance guardrail wrap needed.

nodes.name: Read Weekly Signal Log
nodes.notes: Reads the full log — filtered down to the trailing week in the next step.

nodes.name: Compute Weekly Signal Volume Summary
nodes.notes: SIGNAL_SUMMARY_LOOKBACK_DAYS controls the window — defaults to 7.

nodes.name: Build Weekly Signal Volume Email
nodes.notes: Explicitly sends a 'no signals this week' message rather than a blank digest when nothing came in.

nodes.name: Send Weekly Signal Volume Email
nodes.notes: Internal, firm-wide summary — no guardrail wrap needed.

nodes.name: If Real Signal
nodes.notes: Tag Signals By Practice Area has alwaysOutputData enabled so a zero-match day doesn't halt the digest branch -- but that means it can emit a single placeholder empty item on those days. This guard keeps that placeholder from being written to the Signal Log sheet as a garbage blank row; only items with a real signal_id proceed to logging.

nodes.name: Skip — No Real Signal To Log
nodes.notes: Nothing to log here -- either zero signals matched today (the alwaysOutputData placeholder) or the item is otherwise incomplete.

main.node: Skip — No Real Signal To Log

description: Internal Protomated tool, Authority pillar, not deployed to clients. Runs daily: queries a configured public open-data API (built against the Socrata SODA pattern) for recent business filing/permit/license records, normalizes dataset-specific field names, dedupes against previously seen signals, tags each against a configurable practice-area keyword map, logs matches, and emails a digest to a BD reviewer. Separately, a weekly rollup reports signal volume and top signal types by practice area. Powers Protomated's own BD pipeline and authority content. Replaces manual BD research and paid data vendors.
